newsitem.title: USA: American, pilots resume talks to avert strike.
newsitem.headline: American, pilots resume talks to avert strike.

text.p: American Airlines and its pilots resumed talks Tuesday to try to avert a strike set for midnight Friday that would shut down the carrier and strand hundreds of thousands of passengers.

The contract negotiations, under the auspices of the National Mediation Board, opened on Monday with both sides saying their aim was to reach a deal. Mediators, after the first session, called the bargaining "businesslike, very serious."

The Allied Pilots Association is seeking a pay raise of 11.5 percent and stock options from American, the nation's second largest airline that is a unit of Dallas-based AMR Corp.. American has offered 5 percent.
At issue also is American's plan to add jets to its regional carrier American Eagle and use lower-paid pilots to fly them.
The pilots have said that without a new contract, they would strike at 0001 EST (0501 GMT) on Saturday. The airline carries about 200,000 passengers on 2,200 routes worldwide each day.
American has said a strike would cost it $50 million a day and that it has arranged a bank loan of up to $2 billion to help it through any job action.
AMR stock rose 62.5 cents to $79.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
